**1B.10 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

**Bottom line:** **more dangerous overall than inherited.**  
Bangladesh’s 2024 record includes some narrow positives on nuclear safeguards and nonproliferation, but the year ended with a severe domestic crisis: curfews, internet shutdowns, large-scale deaths, rights abuses, and Hasina’s flight. On balance, the existential-risk posture looks worse at the end of 2024 than at the start.

**Accepted claims**

- **Bangladesh committed to non-proliferation, peaceful nuclear use: FM**
  - **Publisher:** BSS
  - **Date:** April 30, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/186546
  - **Summary:** The foreign minister said Bangladesh would keep high safety and security standards for nuclear plants and welcomed IAEA training and safeguards support. This is a real positive for narrow nuclear-risk management.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.9

- **Bangladesh reaffirms commitment to nuclear non-proliferation, peaceful use**
  - **Publisher:** Dhaka Tribune
  - **Date:** April 30, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/foreign-affairs/345281/bangladesh-reaffirms-commitment-to-nuclear-non-proliferation-peaceful-use
  - **Summary:** Bangladesh said it would maintain transparency, safety, and security for nuclear plants and highlighted IAEA-backed training and capacity building. Again, positive for institutional risk control, but limited to one domain.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9

- **Consider setting up 2nd nuclear power plant**
  - **Publisher:** The Daily Star / UNB
  - **Date:** April 2, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/consider-setting-2nd-nuclear-power-plant-3580751
  - **Summary:** Hasina pushed a second Rooppur plant and directed spent-fuel return formalities to Russia. This suggests back-end custody planning, not recklessness, but it is still a narrow and project-specific improvement.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9, 1B.1

- **Bangladesh nuclear regulators train at Russia’s Novovoronezh NPP**
  - **Publisher:** Nuclear Engineering International
  - **Date:** June 18, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.neimagazine.com/news/bangladesh-nuclear-regulators-train-at-russias-novovoronezh-npp/
  - **Summary:** BAERA inspectors received regulator training. This is evidence of institutional capacity-building rather than purely political control.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9

- **Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant : 48 Bangladeshi specialists complete pre-licensing training**
  - **Publisher:** Daily Country Today
  - **Date:** July 8, 2024
  - **URL:** https://dailycountrytodaybd.com/story/rooppur-nuclear-power-plant-%3A-48-bangladeshi-specialists-complete-pre-licensing-training
  - **Summary:** Specialists completed pre-licensing training and still needed BAERA licenses. That is another sign of technical pipeline discipline.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9

- **Home | Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority**
  - **Publisher:** BAERA
  - **Date:** November 3-7, 2024
  - **URL:** https://baera.gov.bd/
  - **Summary:** The regulator’s homepage references a National Training Course on Safeguards. That is direct official evidence of safeguards-oriented institutional activity.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9, 1B.4

- **Bangladesh army enforces curfew as student-led protests spiral**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** July 20, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-army-enforces-curfew-as-student-led-protests-spiral/2182818/
  - **Summary:** Reuters described internet/text shutdowns and a nationwide curfew as violence escalated. This is a strong negative for overall existential-risk posture because it shows greater opacity and coercion.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** July 22, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153
  - **Summary:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed opponents for the violence. That points toward escalation and poor crisis management, not a safer inherited posture.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations / OHCHR
  - **Date:** July 26, 2024
  - **URL:** https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights
  - **Summary:** The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. This is strong evidence that the year ended with a more dangerous domestic environment.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigns, interim government to be formed**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** August 5, 2024
  - **URL:** https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-pm-sheikh-hasina-resigns-interim-government-to-be-formed/2208572/
  - **Summary:** Reuters reported Hasina fled and an interim government would be formed. That is a clear marker of regime breakdown, which worsens existential-risk posture.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Exclusive-Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina's fate**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** August 6, 2024
  - **URL:** https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302
  - **Summary:** Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce the curfew. This implies Hasina was relying on force in a domestic crisis rather than reducing danger.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5, 1B.7

- **UN Fact-Finding Team Issues Call for Submissions**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations in Bangladesh / OHCHR
  - **Date:** September 16, 2024
  - **URL:** https://bangladesh.un.org/en/278741-un-fact-finding-team-issues-call-submissions
  - **Summary:** The UN opened a fact-finding process on alleged violations from July 1 to August 15, 2024. That strongly corroborates that the year ended in a serious rights and governance crisis.
  - **Question IDs:** 1B.10, 1B.8, 1B.5

**Synthesis**

- **Positive:** Bangladesh did invest in nuclear safeguards, licensing, and IAEA-linked capacity building.
- **Negative:** Those gains were narrow and technical, while the broader 2024 outcome was a major governance collapse with lethal repression and loss of control.
- **Conclusion:** **Hasina left Bangladesh in a more dangerous existential-risk state than she inherited it.**
